Federated LPV · Continuous calibration · Pilot seeds 1301–1303

The trajectories work in the simulator.
The noisy local matrix estimates need more work.

All nine pilot jobs verified. Continuous motion, settling, and clean-data identification pass. With sensor noise, ordinary least squares still fails the matrix-accuracy requirement, especially at low speed. The ten-fleet sharing comparison has not started.

Maneuver / settling checks747 / 747client–speed–profile cells; training and validation both pass
Noise-free accuracy screen747 / 747matrix accuracy, validation prediction and persistence comparison
Strong profile, noisy matrices183 / 24973.5% pass; at least 95% was required
Decision: pause confirmation

Keep the continuous-data direction. Diagnose local identification first.

The pilot does not show a failure of federation: it contains no scientific group-fitting comparison. It identifies a problem earlier in the pipeline, when noisy state and steering observations are converted into local A/B matrices.

Do not relax the screen or substitute noise-free results for the sensor condition. The clean and target-only-noise conditions are useful controls for the next diagnosis.

1. What passed, and what stopped selection?

Each profile covers 249 local fits across three fleets of 30 vehicles. The 95th percentile describes the distribution across those cells; it is not a confidence interval.

Physical envelope observed

How to read “passed”

Every profile satisfies the declared steering, lateral-acceleration and sideslip limits, reaches the intended turn, and has full local regressor rank with acceptable scaled condition number.

Every sensor fit also meets the one-second prediction limit and beats holding the initial state constant. Only the matrix-error condition stops the sensor accuracy screen.

These are simulation checks under instrumented calibration assumptions. They do not certify road safety, ordinary-driving identification, or observer-based sensing.

2. Separate the acquisition and noise effects

Matched row count is not matched driving time. The 36 selected trajectory transitions are spread over the full 20-second excitation window. “All” uses 2,000 consecutive transitions. Reset36 also uses an analytical equilibrium, while the trajectory fits use an empirical quiet-segment center.

Lines show median matrix error at each observed speed, conditional on the filters. The logarithmic axis separates clean-data accuracy from the larger noisy errors.

3. Why does stronger steering leave the same upper tail?

The amplitude is capped at 0.8°. At 10 and 12 m/s, both the standard and strong settings hit that cap and therefore generate identical physical steering and paired noise realizations. Raising the profile label cannot improve these cells.

Strong profile: where the 66 failures occur

62 of 66 failures are at 10–14 m/s. Every 10 and 12 m/s sensor fit fails the 10% matrix-error limit. All 18–30 m/s cells pass.

The clean regressor remains full rank. However, its weakest standardized direction is substantially smaller at low speed. Full rank and a permissive condition-number limit do not establish robustness to measurement noise.

4. Good trajectory prediction can hide a poor dynamics matrix

For the strongest profile, all 249 noisy fits predict the separate chirp satisfactorily, even though 66 have excessive matrix error. A validation maneuver explores a restricted set of state/input combinations; errors in individual coefficients can compensate along that motion.

Sensor condition, using the filters above. Hover over a point for client, speed and errors. The shaded area passes prediction but fails matrix accuracy. Both axes are logarithmic. Prediction uses a one-second free run from a common exact initial state; it does not test state-estimation error.

Why measurement noise can bias this regression

Ignoring centering and nonlinear residuals for this explanation, let measured states and steering be x̃k = xk + νk and ũk = uk + ηk. The equation expressed in measured variables is

x̃k+1 = A x̃k + B ũk + [νk+1 − Aνk − Bηk].

The regression residual contains the same current measurement errors as the regressors. Its correlation with them can bias ordinary least squares. The clean → target-only noise → coherent sensor contrast strongly supports this explanation, but the current pilot does not separately isolate state noise, steering noise, temporal noise reuse, and noisy centering.

See MathWorks’ identification example on measurement noise, output-error models and instrumental variables. It motivates alternatives; it is not a guarantee that a particular IV estimator will work with these weakly excited data.

5. Inspect the individual fits

Sensor fits sorted by decreasing matrix error. Click a row to compare its estimated matrix entries with the reference. Filters above apply here too.

6. The next focused step

  1. Keep this pilot frozen. Use its saved trajectories and targets to investigate noise sensitivity; the ten confirmation fleets remain untouched.
  2. Separate the noise sources on the same physical motion. Compare state-only, steering-only and centering effects. This identifies what an estimator must handle.
  3. Test one noise-aware local estimator against OLS. A carefully constructed instrumental-variable or output-error fit is a candidate. Verify instruments/noise assumptions and local matrix accuracy, not just one-step prediction.
  4. If low-speed directions remain weak, revise the input spectrum. Compare a small predefined low-speed bandwidth change within the same steering/rate envelope. The amplitude cap explains why simply increasing the current profile is ineffective at 10 and 12 m/s.
  5. Freeze a passing calibration/estimator combination, then run the fleet comparison. Reassess Global and Smooth Local alongside Federated on the same new targets.

No alternative estimator was fitted and no new trajectory campaign was run for this analysis. Recommendations are prospective. More samples alone do not establish that measurement-error bias is removed.

Provenance and scope

Audited: nine payload hashes and source locks; all 3,735 cell–condition matrix errors independently recomputed from saved targets and references; the saved CSV and the frozen selection reproduced. No historical artifact was rewritten.

There are three independent pilot fleets. Filtered cell summaries are descriptive and should not be treated as 747 independent experimental replications. No confidence interval for a sharing benefit is available here.
